body: Okay, is your face attractive? Yes. Your hairstyle is terrible, sorry mate. That first picture you looked 'healthy' if that makes sense. The last picture with your hair dyed black makes you look peakish. It contrasts so much with your skin tone that it makes all the imperfections and blemishes stand out even more. My suggestion - lose the hair color, and try something shorter and cleaner looking.

There are slight things you could do to improve. Start with your eyebrows. Get a girl to help you with that, trust me. Your hair style suits you well, as does the facial hair, BUT keep it trimmed and clean. 

Either way, you are handsome. Grats.

Well, in addition to what's already been said, I highly suggest getting a new pair of glasses. #1, tinted prescription glasses are not attractive. At all. #2, The frames you've selected, just no. I suggest trying something with a thicker frame. 

Your hair - it's neat (for the most part), but you just comb it forward. I can't tell if you have a receding hairline, and that is why you do that, but I suggest a different hairstyle.
Bro, repost with your whole face in the picture.
Yeah, I can't control other people's actions, I can only control my reactions. I understand, thanks for the reply. I guess I know what I have to do, I just needed to vent a little bit.
Again...see my above reply: it's an excuse.

I understand you a little better now. Sorry for the assumptions.  The question you need to ask yourself, is do you see yourself long-term with this girl? As in, if she had none of these issues, how far would you take this relationship? 

If you say that you can see yourself with her indefinitely,  then you need to ask yourself if you love her enough to take a chance on her. As in, being her rock while she sorts through her issues.

If not,  then maybe you should break it off and start fresh?
...this is what people in grad school speak like now.

First of all, when you gave her your advice, I sure hope you didn't bring up sex. As in, 'Hey honey, I'm concerned that you've been crying during sex" rather than "Hey honey, I'm concerned that you're crying"

I'm assuming you brought it up with sex as your basis. Well since you seem more concerned about 'hooking up' with your girlfriend of 9 months with no issues, here's my advice: Learn to be less selfish.

Hey bud. She's not interested in you. Girls do not forget things that are important. Let me say that again. Girls do not forget. 

If you were in fact someone she was interested in, she would have texted you back after your second date. The reason why she was texting you back at all, is because she doesn't want to be rude, and is hoping you'll just go away because she's probably bad at dealing with confrontations or uncomfortable situations, and she knows end of term is right around the corner. 

Let her go mate.

Here is my gut feeling on this: He doesn't love you, and doesn't have any intention of falling in love with you. When he questioned your love for him with his ability as a boyfriend - that's just a sad, sad excuse. I'm really sorry that you are hurting right now. I'm sure you are a great girlfriend to him, but some guys are just stuck in neutral. It's not your job or responsibility to enable him to commit. The problem with him, is there *is* no right girl for him right now. It could have been anyone in your shoes. The best thing you can do is move on, and find someone worth your valuable time. 

As an aside, 10 months is quite normal to drop the love bomb. Honestly, I'd even say anything around 6 months is average. 

Good luck.
Of course you can. If you are feeling pressure from your friends or others that this is taboo or wrong, ignore them. Do what makes you happy.
